evidence_checks.located_span: My mother says this tote hurts her shoulder.
evidence_checks.note: The shoulder pain belongs to the commenter's mother, reported second-hand. The commenter's own experience is the opposite: 'Mine feels comfortable, even with a laptop.'
evidence_checks.usage_situation: carrying tote on shoulder, with laptop

scope_issue: Takes a pain report about a third party (the mother) and assigns it to the commenter as first-hand experience. The commenter explicitly says their own tote feels comfortable. 'This tote' and 'Mine' are not tied to an exact SKU; only the source metadata names the Aster Levant Tote.
reasoning: The cited span is the mother's experience, relayed by the commenter. In the next sentence the commenter says their own tote feels comfortable even with a laptop, which directly contradicts the claim that the commenter personally had shoulder pain.
speaker_attribution: a person the author reports (mother) for the pain; author first-hand for comfort

evidence_checks.located_span: My mother says this tote hurts her shoulder. Mine feels comfortable, even with a laptop.
evidence_checks.note: The first sentence is the mother's complaint, reported by the commenter. The second sentence is the commenter's own comfortable experience. The cited span covers only the first half; the second half is in the same comment.
evidence_checks.usage_situation: carrying tote on shoulder, with laptop

reasoning: The claim gets both parts right: the mother's complaint is reported second-hand, and the commenter's own comfort is first-hand. 'Hurts her shoulder' fairly supports 'shoulder discomfort'. The claim makes no product-model, demographic or causal statement beyond the text.
speaker_attribution: a person the author reports (mother) plus author first-hand

evidence_checks.note: 'This.' agrees with the parent comment, and the parent says: 'I stopped taking the large tote to the office. I only use my backpack now.' So the reply backs giving up the large tote for office commuting, not using it.

scope_issue: Reverses what the reply agrees with. The parent stopped using the large tote and switched to a backpack. 'This.' gives no personal experience of the replier's own, and nothing ties the parent's 'large tote' to the Aster Levant Tote.
reasoning: The reply means something only through its parent comment. The parent describes stopping use of a large tote for the office and switching to a backpack. A one-word 'This.' at most agrees with that, which is the opposite of endorsing a large tote for office commuting.
speaker_attribution: unknown (replier's agreement with a different author's first-hand statement)

evidence_checks.note: Only the comment itself was captured (COMMENT_ONLY). It does not mention a zipper, a failure or the tote, and no parent text is provided.

scope_issue: The claim invents both the subject (zipper failure) and a confirmation. Without the parent there is no way to know what 'This.' refers to.
reasoning: A bare 'This.' with no captured parent context cannot show that a zipper failed, or that the replier experienced or confirmed anything about the product. The zipper failure and the personal confirmation are not in the source.

evidence_checks.note: Only the comment itself was captured. It does not mention shoulder pain, a tote or the product, and the parent it answers is not provided.

scope_issue: The claim supplies the subject (shoulder pain from the tote), which appears nowhere in the source. 'Same here' cannot be read without the missing parent comment.
reasoning: 'Same here — every single time' signals agreement with something unseen. With only the comment captured, nothing ties it to shoulder pain or to the tote. So the source cannot back a first-hand claim of shoulder pain.

evidence_checks.located_span: I received this bag free and earn commission from links.
evidence_checks.note: The author says they got the bag free and earn affiliate commission, which directly contradicts 'independent uncompensated'. The only product opinion in the comment is 'I love the pockets.'

scope_issue: 'Independent uncompensated' is contradicted by the disclosure of a free product and affiliate commission. 'Best tote for organization' turns 'I love the pockets' into a comparative superlative that the text never makes. 'Confirms the brand' generalises from one bag to the whole brand.
reasoning: The cited span is a compensation disclosure: a free bag plus commission on links. That shows the speaker is not independent or uncompensated. The positive part, 'I love the pockets', is a single sponsored remark about pockets, not a claim that the brand is the best for organization.
